spec.title: vscode-extension PROP-006: Licensing - where this family states a licence

status.comment: the type's answer to the twelfth area of the contract, written and implemented 2026-11-01 by the campaign licensing-extension-family from the measured behaviour of the family's packager and the state of the extension pilot; the profile, the header layout, the writing of the surfaces, the annotation of own files and the checks stay in the engine (modules/codkit/PROP-019)

p.VSX-LICENSING-AREA: The type declares the capability `licensing` and answers the area (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LICENSING`) as a function of `typeConfig`, like every answer of the family (PROP-001 `VSX-CONFIGURED-TYPE`): `headerStyle: line` - the sources of this family carry no header of their own, and the four-line form is the one `gen brand` already writes into the own layer, so own code keeps the shape it has; `licenceFileDirectory` the configured `extensionRoot` (the root itself for a repository that is one extension); `componentLicenceDirectory` `<extensionRoot>/licenses`; `subsystem: config`; the field, the upstream licence file, the exclusion and the guard stated below; no renderings, because the family has no installer. A type writes nothing: the engine lays headers out from the profile, writes the overlay, the add-file patches, the exclusion patch and the guard, and checks them back.

p.VSX-LICENCE-FIELD: One field names the licence: the key `license` of the extension manifest (`<extensionRoot>/package.json`, the first overlay target of PROP-003 `VSX-MANIFEST-OVERLAY`), role `expression` - the own SPDX identifier the profile declares, the same meaning the editor family gives the key. The manifest is open to an overlay whole, so no scalar rule of the target is needed. No field names the licence file: the family's manifest has none, and the packager finds the file by name.

p.DECISION-VSX-LICENCE-FIELD-IS-THE-EXPRES: **Decision:** the manifest's `license` carries the own expression, never `SEE LICENSE IN <file>`. **Why:** the contract asks the field for the expression and the profile is its single source (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#GEN-LICENSING` (1)); which file the archive carries as its licence is settled by the exclusion of `VSX-DISTRIBUTABLE-EXCLUSION`, not by a pointer in the field. **Considered and rejected:** `SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md` (a file pointer where the contract asks for the expression, and the upstream's text would still ship at the archive root as a second licence); both licence files side by side (the packager takes the upstream's, `VSX-LICENCE-FILE-IN-EXTENSION-ROOT`). **When to revisit:** a packager that reads the licence of the archive from the field alone - then the field may carry what that packager reads and the exclusion becomes unnecessary.

files.title: 2. The licence file, the component licences and the archive

p.VSX-LICENCE-FILE-IN-EXTENSION-ROOT: The product's licence file lives in the extension root under the name the product chose (`product.licenseFile` of its declaration, `LICENSE.md` by default): the archive is packed from the extension root, and the family's packager (vsce 4.0.0 at the pilot's pin, measured 2026-11-01) takes as the licence asset of the archive the first file, in sorted order, named `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md` or `LICENSE.txt` - unless the manifest's `license` reads `SEE LICENSE IN <file>` - and renames a bare `LICENSE` to `LICENSE.txt` inside the archive. A monorepo's tree root is not packed and is no place for the file.

p.VSX-COMPONENT-LICENCES: `<extensionRoot>/licenses/` is the component directory: the ignore file of the family excludes build inputs by pattern and not this directory, so the archive carries it. One component: the upstream's licence file of the extension root - `typeConfig.licensing.upstreamLicenceFile`, `LICENSE` by default - byte for byte at the pin, under the component `typeConfig.licensing.upstreamComponent`, `upstream` by default, so the file is `licenses/LICENSE-UPSTREAM.md` until a product names the upstream's open build (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#LICENCE-DOCUMENT-NAMES`). No component of the tool: the family delivers no runtime library (PROP-001 `VSX-ABSENCES`), nothing of the tool is compiled into the product, and the tool's notice copy under the own root is not the library (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#GEN-LICENSING` (3)).

p.DECISION-VSX-UPSTREAM-COMPONENT-FROM-CON: **Decision:** the upstream's licence file and its component name come from the configuration, with the defaults above. **Why:** the family cannot know the upstream's name - every product of the family has a different upstream - and a type answers from the configuration, never from the tree (PROP-001 `VSX-CONFIGURED-TYPE`); a default keeps the answer well-formed for a patch set that declared nothing, so that the upstream's text is never hidden once the exclusion removes its file from the archive. **Considered and rejected:** reading the manifest's `name` at the pin (the tree); a required key (an unconfigured patch set would answer an empty list, which hides the upstream's text altogether). **When to revisit:** a product whose upstream ships several licence files - then the key takes a list.

p.VSX-DISTRIBUTABLE-EXCLUSION: The archive leaves out the upstream's licence file: the type answers one exclusion of the distributable - the ignore file `<extensionRoot>/.vscodeignore` and the entry naming the upstream's licence file - which `gen licensing` writes as a marker-block patch of the ignore file (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#GEN-LICENSING` (6), the form of PROP-004 `MR-FORM-KEY`) and `verify` and the guard check back. The product's licence file is then the only file the packager's rule matches, and the upstream's terms still travel with the archive under `licenses/`, which is what its licence asks for; the upstream's file in the tree is never edited or renamed. An upstream that names its files in the manifest's `files` field instead of an ignore file is a product fact to record in the product's repository; the packager reads the field then, and the exclusion is written where the product says.

p.VSX-LICENCE-GUARD: The guard is written at `delta/own/test/licence.leftovers.test.ts`, beside the brand guard (PROP-005 `VSX-BRAND-LEFTOVER-GUARD`), in the words of the declared own-test runner as the brand guard is (`describe`/`test` for bun, vitest and jest, `suite`/`test` for vscode-test, `describe`/`it` for mocha), with no preamble unless the family's lint of a product asks for one at the first render - recorded in the product's repository, and here once a second product asks. Its `runnerDirectory` is the extension root (the root itself for a repository that is one extension): the own tests of a workspace package run in the extension root, and the engine's one template resolves the tree root from its working directory through it (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#LICENCE-GUARD`).
